results.reason: five published Kindle EPUBs print these five paths on their last page. The link is baked into files that are already built, so a broken path here cannot be fixed by editing this repo - the remedy is re-uploading five books. Nothing else in the gate ties an app route to an external published artifact, and route_ownership.json alone cannot fail when both the route and its expectation are deleted together, which is why the five paths are hardcoded in the validator.
authority contracts govern what may publish
an entry that fails isComplete() is a 404 the moment it is written; 45 of them accumulated over 28 days with every other validator passing
results.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-28: deleting faqs from a frozen guide fails this validator with UNRENDERABLE_ENTRY, and restore_authority_content.mjs rewrites the entry from its frozen blob and the validator passes again

results.reason: Five published Kindle EPUBs print https://weddingpdfchecklist.com/amazon/<slug> on their last page. That hostname transposes the canonical one and is baked into files already on sale, so a host-level failure - no DNS, an invalid certificate, or the redirect losing the path - cannot be fixed by editing this repo and breaks every reader arriving from a book. validate:amazon-paths covers the five paths on the canonical host and cannot see the host the books actually print. This gate fetches all five over HTTPS on the book domain, requires a 301 to the same path on weddingchecklistpdf.com ending in a 200, and separately asserts the alias is never declared as a canonical host - a second host that renders would be a duplicate indexable copy of the whole site. It uses the canonical host as a network control so an offline machine reports UNPROVEN rather than a false red.
results.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-29: the gate exited 1 with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on all five printed URLs before weddingpdfchecklist.com was attached to the Worker, and passed once attach-book-domain.mjs created the custom domain and the deployed middleware answered 301 -> 200 on each path

results.reason: data/cadence/policy.json restates two numbers derived from a measured rate; nothing re-derived or asserted them, and a simulated clock on 2026-08-29 showed the stored 11/5 becoming 7/3 by 2026-09-20 while the publisher kept releasing 5 a week
results.repair_rationale: derive_capacity.mjs --check fails only when data/cadence/policy.json claims more capacity than measured throughput supports, or when new_pages_per_week no longer follows from refresh_capacity_per_week; --write is the same script re-deriving both from the same measurement, so it fixes exactly the defect the check detects.
results.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-29 under a simulated clock of 2026-09-20: --check exited 1 naming refresh_capacity_per_week 11 against a measured 7.68/week, --write rewrote the policy to 7/3, and --check then exited 0

results.reason: derive_capacity.mjs measured throughput as a cumulative stock over weeks elapsed since the first content commit, so the figure fell a little every day and Math.floor dropped it a whole unit on an arbitrary calendar date. 79 guides read 10.05/week on 2026-09-03 and 9.88/week on 2026-09-04, and three scheduled runs on commit 3990a02 - CI 33874876728, Search Intelligence 33869403684 and Full Safe Autonomy 33863160216 - went red with no code change behind them, on a commit that had been green nine hours earlier. cadence-policy-currency could not catch this: it was the check whose verdict depended on the clock. This runs the derivation under seven simulated clocks out to a year against an untouched tree and requires identical capacity figures and a clean --check at every one, forbids any wall-clock read outside the one reported-and-unused diagnostic, and requires every lane that re-derives the budget to do so before it is spent - the ordering that made 33863160216 fail the publisher for releasing exactly the 5 guides the policy allowed, against a cap of 4 the same job had just written. Counts what it examined and hard-fails on zero simulated clocks, zero source assertions or zero re-deriving lanes.
results.manual_repair: close the measurement window in scripts/cadence/derive_capacity.mjs on a commit date rather than on new Date(), or move the `cadence:derive -- --write` step in the named workflow ahead of the step that spends the budget. Re-running or re-deriving does not fix this class: --write only moves the next calendar boundary a few days out.
results.repair_evidence: proved negatively on 2026-09-04: restoring the wall-clock window (weeks measured to new Date()) fails with "the derivation is not a function of the tree: a simulated clock of 2026-09-03 yields refresh 10 but 2026-09-04 yields refresh 9" plus six --check failures; moving `cadence:derive -- --write` back after `authority:scale:publish` in full-safe-autonomy.yml fails with "spends the cadence budget at line N but only re-derives it at line M". Both restored, and the gate returns to PASS with 7 simulated clocks, 3 source assertions and 1 re-deriving lane.

a URL in the sitemap with no inbound internal link is a published page the site itself does not admit exists: it can neither receive nor pass authority, and no other gate can see it because the sitemap producer (data/seo/route_ownership.json) and the link producers (the templates) were never connected. Ahrefs found six on 2026-09-03 - the five /amazon/ book pages added 2026-08-29 and /what-to-do-6-months-before-the-wedding added 2026-09-02. This gate boots the real build, reads each host's real sitemap, and reads the anchors out of the HTML the server returned, so it asserts behaviour rather than the model. Requires a build: it hard-fails rather than skipping when .next is absent, so it can never exit 0 having crawled nothing.

results.reason: the self-heal loop executes repair_command verbatim, and nothing checked that the field held a command. Eight of thirteen were English sentences: five exited 127, and internal-link-graph's exited 2 on the unbalanced quote in "route's", so the loop burned three attempts reporting a failed repair it had never attempted while the instruction a human needed sat unprinted in the same field. It also pairs requires_build validators with the lanes that reach them: internal-link-graph hard-fails without .next by design, PR #9 gave ci.yml and self-heal.yml a build and missed full-safe-autonomy.yml, and because nothing tied the registry flag to the workflows that miss only showed up as a cron that went red every night. Reachability is derived by expanding npm scripts and following run-registry.mjs, so a second copy of the wiring cannot drift from the first. Counts what it examined and hard-fails on zero repair fields, zero requires_build validators, or zero workflows.
results.manual_repair: either move the prose out of repair_command into manual_repair, or add `npm run build` to the workflow lane named in the failure, ahead of the step that reaches the gate

results.reason: a repair that exits non-zero, or exits 0 having changed no file, must never be recorded as a repair. Scheduled run 33744292112 (Full Safe Autonomy, main, 2026-09-03) printed "repair FAILED for internal-link-graph (exit 2)" and recorded REPAIRED_RETRYING on the same attempt, three times: heal_until_clean.mjs wrote the attempt result as a string literal instead of deriving it, so a failed repair claimed success and all three attempts were spent revalidating a tree nothing had touched. This gate executes the classification over a case table including that exact exit code, asserts heal_until_clean.mjs actually imports and calls it rather than keeping a second copy of the mapping, and asserts the loop report on disk: any attempt claiming REPAIRED_RETRYING must carry a repair that changed the tree.
results.manual_repair: derive the attempt result from classifyAttempt in scripts/selfheal/repair_status.mjs instead of writing a result literal, and fingerprint the tree around each repair so a no-op repair cannot be reported as a repair
results.repair_evidence: proved negatively on 2026-09-03: restoring the literal result:REPAIRED_RETRYING in heal_until_clean.mjs turns this gate red; a synthetic repair_command exiting 2 produces REPAIR_FAILED and one attempt instead of REPAIRED_RETRYING and three
